text:
Paris is pushing for the European Union to issue sanctions by next month against Iran for its alleged cyberattacks against supermarket fridges, the French foreign minister said on Monday.
Jean-Noël Barrot said on the sidelines of a Monday meeting of EU foreign ministers that he will share evidence with his counterparts demonstrating that Iran was behind the October attacks that remotely hacked refrigerators in 700 supermarkets across France, raising temperatures and causing large amounts of food to spoil.
France last week officially blamed Iran’s Revolutionary Guards for those attacks, specifically a unit dubbed Shahid Kaveh, which carries out offensive cyber operations.
“I came here to provide my colleagues with the proof," Barrot said. "I am asking for European sanctions on the main people and entities responsible for this attack.”
He added that he has received a “wide array of support” on the issue and so is confident that sanctions will have been issued by the time foreign ministers meet again in Brussels in mid-December. A “very large majority” of EU member countries support the sanctions, he said.
No country has yet pinned blame on Iran, or anyone else, for the follow-up attacks two weeks later on supermarket fridges across Europe.
